rules_evaluated.evidence: Body line 38: "Ask Claude to run `git merge-base m4/<slug> <the branch you cut it from>` and fork from that commit. It is where the branch left the trunk, so it is where the run started." Live-tested with a throwaway repo replicating this exercise's exact branch shape (trunk commit → `git checkout -b m4/<slug>` → append Run-coordinates block to task.md → commit "M4 starting point" → further M4 work commits). `git merge-base m4/<slug> main` returns the TRUNK commit that predates "M4 starting point", not the "M4 starting point" commit itself — confirmed empirically (merge_base == trunk_sha, merge_base != m4start_sha). The claimed equivalence ("where the branch left the trunk" = "where the run started") is off by exactly one commit, because `prompt:ae101-m4-commit-starting-point` appends the Run-coordinates block to task.md and commits it BEFORE any M4 work begins — so the branch's true git fork-point is the parent of the designated "run started" commit, not that commit.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Non-blocking in practice: since "M4 starting point" only adds a task.md metadata diff (no source changes) before the M4 work proper begins, forking from merge-base yields functionally identical source code to forking from "M4 starting point" — and this rung only fires when the coordinates block is already unrecoverable anyway, so the missing metadata is moot. Consider softening the wording from an exact equivalence ("it is where the run started") to an approximation ("it's the commit just before the run started — close enough that the code is the same") so the claim matches what merge-base actually returns.
